profile.reading: This Expedient facility, named BWI1 on the operator own page and Owings Mills in this registry, is located at 11155 Red Run Boulevard, Suite 200, Owings Mills, Maryland 21117. The operator own facility page describes 22,000 square feet of data center space, including 8,800 square feet of raised floor, a critical IT load of 800 kW, and 3.5 MW of total generator capacity, on a 2N UPS configuration. The facility connects to 6 on net carriers. The page states SOC 1, SOC 2, HIPAA, PCI DSS, and HITRUST compliance. This facility, marketed by Expedient as BWI1, is one of two buildings the operator groups under its Baltimore market, alongside the separate Tidepoint facility in downtown Baltimore tracked elsewhere in this registry; both share one operator regional page but carry distinct addresses, critical IT loads, and specifications rather than being treated as a single undifferentiated campus. Expedient traces to the October 2003 acquisition of Stargate Business, a Pittsburgh-based company, after which Expedient formally designated Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania as its headquarters in May 2004, citing Stargate's established infrastructure and the roughly 70 percent of Expedient's workforce already based there; the company was at that time privately owned within the Continental Broadband family under Landmark Communications, and its ownership has since changed to AMP Capital, an Australian investment firm, as its investment sponsor. Owings Mills sits in the Baltimore metro's northwest suburbs, a secondary Maryland colocation submarket to the denser Northern Virginia cluster tracked extensively elsewhere in this registry. No year-opened date specific to this facility was located in sourcing reachable this session. No further public ownership or tenant-mix detail specific to this building was located this session.
profile.capacity_note: Operator also states 3.5 MW of total generator capacity, a backup power figure distinct from the 800 kW critical IT load recorded here.

reading.body:
Expedient Owings Mills has 800 kW of critical IT load, which translates to roughly 20 racks at typical AI training density, too small to constitute meaningful AI infrastructure.

The facility is built for regulated enterprise and healthcare workloads rather than compute-intensive applications. Its SOC 1, SOC 2, HIPAA, PCI DSS, and HITRUST certifications, combined with six on-net carrier connections, identify it as designed for traffic redundancy and compliance, not for the sustained power draw and thermal management that AI training requires. The 3.5 MW of backup generator capacity exceeds the 800 kW critical load, confirming the site is sized for continuous operation of traditional data center workloads.

Maryland publishes capacity figures for only three of its eleven mapped data center facilities, totaling 9.3 MW. Owings Mills ranks second among these three. At this scale, Maryland's documented data center capacity remains marginal relative to the power requirements of current AI scaling. Whether this facility will play any role in AI infrastructure depends on whether Expedient repurposes it for compute workloads or whether the published figure omits capacity installed after the operator's specification was released.
